name: Play a colorless land on turn 1-2 when nothing in hand unlocks anything
intent: On turn 1 or 2, once none of open-land-unlocks, open-shock-unlocks, open-fetch-unlocks or open-fetch-unlocks-shock apply and no other hand card is already affordable, still play the land drop - any land beats holding it back with nothing to protect. The select and true count both carry colors_any:[colorless], excluding Dryad Arbor: Arbor never unlocks anything (summoning sick the turn it enters, so open-land-unlocks already leaves it alone), but 'Dryad Arbor' sorts before every other land in this deck by name, and this play's own prefer order is already at the 4-tier cap with no room for a fifth 'Arbor last' tier - so ties any would hand it Arbor first on a tied board unless the candidate pool excludes Arbor outright. An Arbor-only hand (no other land at all) is left to the seat rather than forced to play Arbor. Prefers a surveil land (Underground Mortuary) first and keeps the surveilled card; then a shockland, life declined - a paid shock is real mana this turn, strictly better to hold open than an already-untapped fetch that produces nothing until cracked (item 9, 2026-09-14 review batch: tiers 2/3 swapped from the original FETCH-then-SHOCK order); then a fetch, held everywhere else for a target-rich turn but taken here since nothing else is better; then a basic. The false list's own fetch key narrows from unlocks_by_search to unlocks_by_basic_search (item 4), matching open-fetch-unlocks' own narrowed true key exactly, so this play only stands down for F when F would actually fire; a second entry names the broader unlocks_by_search key too (item 4, 2026-09-14), matching open-fetch-unlocks-shock's own true key now that the two fetch plays no longer share one selector. Only turns 1-2, land drop available, mine, precombat main, empty stack.
